question: Read me your mobile number digit by digit. Is 07944 512946 right, and is it the number you want ringing?
why: The old site linked a number two digits short, so tapping it on a phone failed or rang the wrong person. The rebuild renders the label and the link from one constant — that constant needs to be right.
where: content/site.ts → PHONE_E164, then set PHONE_CONFIRMED = true

question: What do you charge for a Saturday session now — is it still £55 an hour, or £150 for three hours? And how do you want to handle travel?
why: The price is printed in type on /workshops as a trust signal. The figures on the old site are from 2024 and have not been re-confirmed.
where: content/pricing.ts — correct the figures, then set confirmed = true

question: Can we go through your photographs and group them into eight to twelve jobs? For each one: where it was, roughly what year, what the customer wanted, and what you actually did — starting with the preparation.
why: The single biggest fix in the rebuild. The old portfolio was around a hundred untitled images in no order, several of them duplicated. Named jobs with a location and a colour list are what somebody comparing decorators is actually looking for.
where: content/projects/*.mdx — one file per job, copied from _TEMPLATE.mdx

question: For each kitchen, which paints did you use — make, colour name and finish? If you cannot remember exactly, say so and we will leave it off.
why: Colours render as a specimen strip under each job. In front of this audience a wrong paint name is worse than no paint name, so unconfirmed colours are omitted rather than guessed.

question: We need your photographs out of the Wix media manager at full size — the originals, not the copies the website serves.
why: The site is photography-led and runs images full width. The versions Wix serves are cropped, resized and re-encoded, and will look soft at the sizes used here.

question: Can you send the Google reviews from Janet Leclercq, Andrew Waugh and Stella Steele — the full text, copied exactly?
why: The three reviews are set as pull quotes. Their wording has not been reproduced from memory, so each renders as an empty frame until the exact text arrives.

question: What is the link to your Google Business Profile?
why: The reviews link out to the profile so a customer can check them, and it goes in the structured data. On the old site all three credits pointed at the same contributor, so two of the three linked to the wrong person.

question: How far do you travel, and which villages do you work in most? Anywhere you would rather not go?
why: The site says Chester and Cheshire and nothing more specific, because naming a village Neil does not cover would be worse than naming none at all.

question: Do you want an email address on the site, and which one?
why: There is no email address anywhere on the old site, so none is published here.

question: When somebody fills the form in, where should it land — an email, a text message, or both?
why: The form is built and works without JavaScript, but nothing is wired to deliver it. Until it is, an enquiry is written to the server log and goes no further.
where: src/lib/enquiry.ts → deliverEnquiry(), then set DELIVERY_CONFIGURED = true

question: What hours are you happy to be rung on?
why: No opening hours are published anywhere on the old site, so none are claimed here.

question: Are you insured, and do you belong to any trade body or hold any qualifications you would want mentioned?
why: Nothing is claimed on the old site, so nothing is claimed here. If any of it exists it is worth saying plainly.

question: Do you have Facebook or Instagram pages you keep up to date?
why: They go in the structured data as sameAs links, which helps Google connect the site to the Business Profile.

question: Read the site through and tell me anything that is not how you actually work — the order you do a kitchen in, what you say about preparation, anything that does not sound like you.
why: Every word is written in Neil's first person. The method described is standard practice for the work, but it is put in his mouth, and it should be his before it goes live.
